nodes.name: Client OAuth
nodes.summary: httpx2 auth hook that runs the authorization-code flow, stores tokens, and attaches Bearer headers.
nodes.detail: Seven source files under src/mcp/client/auth/. The public entry point is OAuthClientProvider (oauth2.py), a RedirectAwareAuth subclass that plugs into httpx2 as an async auth hook. It drives a five-step flow on every 401 or scope step-up: protected-resource-metadata discovery (RFC 9728 / SEP-985), authorization-server-metadata discovery (RFC 8414), scope selection, client registration or URL-based client-ID (CIMD), and the authorization-code exchange with PKCE. Tokens are stored through the TokenStorage protocol. utils.py contains the stateless helpers called at each step (URL construction, metadata parsing, scope merging, issuer comparison). exceptions.py defines the three exception types. extensions/ holds two machine-to-machine grant providers: client_credentials and identity_assertion (SEP-990 leg 2).

nodes.name: Server OAuth
nodes.summary: Starlette handlers, middleware and routes that implement an OAuth 2.0 authorization server inside an MCP server.
nodes.detail: Sixteen source files under src/mcp/server/auth/. The integration surface is create_auth_routes() (routes.py), which wires up to five Starlette routes: well-known metadata, /authorize, /token, /register (optional), /revoke (optional). Each route is backed by a typed handler class (handlers/). Token verification for resource-server mode uses BearerAuthBackend (middleware/bearer_auth.py) wrapped in Starlette's AuthenticationMiddleware. AuthContextMiddleware stores the resulting AccessToken in a contextvar. The provider.py protocol describes all callbacks a server implementation must supply; settings.py carries the flat AuthSettings configuration.

nodes.name: Shared auth models
nodes.summary: Pydantic models for OAuth tokens, client metadata, server metadata and resource metadata shared by client and server.
nodes.detail: Two files. shared/auth.py defines OAuthToken (RFC 6749 §5.1), OAuthClientMetadata, OAuthClientInformationFull (RFC 7591), OAuthMetadata (RFC 8414), ProtectedResourceMetadata (RFC 9728), AuthorizationCodeResult, and the error helpers InvalidScopeError and InvalidRedirectUriError. shared/auth_utils.py provides resource_url_from_server_url (RFC 8707 canonical form), check_resource_allowed (hierarchical path matching), and calculate_token_expiry.

nodes.name: Client OAuth2 provider
nodes.summary: httpx2 auth hook implementing the full OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with PKCE, token storage and refresh.
nodes.detail: OAuthClientProvider extends RedirectAwareAuth (shared/_httpx_utils.py) and is the primary httpx2 auth class. Its async generator _auth_flow() first loads stored tokens, tries a refresh if the access token is expired, adds the Bearer header, sends the request, and on 401 or scope step-up runs all five discovery and registration steps before retrying. OAuthContext is a dataclass holding all runtime state: server URL, metadata, client info, tokens and an anyio lock that serialises concurrent requests. PKCEParameters generates a 128-character verifier and S256 challenge. check_registration_usable() rejects a dynamic registration whose assigned token-endpoint auth method cannot be exercised by this flow.
facts: code_verifier is 128 characters from ASCII letters, digits and -._~
token_expiry is checked with time.time() <= token_expiry_time
Lock serialises concurrent token refreshes and full re-auth
Resource parameter included only when PRM is present or protocol >= 2025-06-18

nodes.name: OAuthClientProvider
nodes.summary: httpx2 Auth subclass that runs the OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow on demand.
nodes.detail: Constructed with server_url, OAuthClientMetadata, a TokenStorage, optional redirect/callback handlers, an optional client_metadata_url (URL-based client ID per CIMD), and an optional validate_resource_url override. On first use _initialize() reads tokens and client info from storage. The auth generator handles token refresh, adds the Authorization header, and on 401 triggers the full five-step flow. Implements RedirectAwareAuth so httpx2 drives the generator: each yield sends one request and receives its response.

nodes.name: OAuthContext
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding all mutable OAuth state for one provider instance: server URL, discovered metadata, client info, tokens and expiry.
nodes.detail: Holds server_url, client_metadata, storage, redirect_handler, callback_handler, client_metadata_url, and all discovered/minted state: protected_resource_metadata, oauth_metadata, auth_server_url, protocol_version, client_info, current_tokens, token_expiry_time, and an anyio.Lock. Helper methods: get_resource_url() (uses PRM resource if valid per RFC 8707), should_include_resource_param(), prepare_token_auth() (selects Basic/Post/none), is_token_valid(), can_refresh_token(), update_token_expiry(), clear_tokens().

nodes.name: PKCEParameters
nodes.summary: Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) parameter pair: 128-character verifier and its SHA-256 / base64url challenge.
nodes.detail: Pydantic model with code_verifier (43-128 characters) and code_challenge (43-128 characters). The class method generate() creates a 128-character random verifier from ASCII letters, digits and -._~, computes SHA-256, and base64url-encodes the digest without padding for the S256 challenge.

nodes.name: TokenStorage
nodes.summary: Protocol specifying four async methods for persisting OAuth tokens and client registration across restarts.
nodes.detail: Protocol (structural subtyping) with get_tokens() -> OAuthToken | None, set_tokens(tokens), get_client_info() -> OAuthClientInformationFull | None, and set_client_info(client_info). Implementations may store data in memory, on disk, in a database, or in a keychain. The in-memory implementation in the docs_src example holds tokens and client_info as instance attributes.

nodes.name: check_registration_usable()
nodes.summary: Validates that a completed dynamic client registration returns credentials this flow can actually use.
nodes.detail: Called immediately after handle_registration_response() with the parsed OAuthClientInformationFull. Raises OAuthRegistrationError if the server assigned a token_endpoint_auth_method this flow does not implement (private_key_jwt in particular), or if it assigned a secret-based method but issued no client_secret. This surfaces the error before any interactive authorization begins rather than producing an opaque failure at the token endpoint.

nodes.name: _perform_authorization_code_grant()
nodes.summary: Builds the authorization URL with PKCE and state, calls the redirect and callback handlers, and returns the auth code and verifier.
nodes.detail: Generates PKCEParameters and a 32-byte random state token. Builds the authorization URL with response_type=code, PKCE challenge (S256), optional resource parameter (RFC 8707), and scope; adds prompt=consent when offline_access is requested (OpenID Connect requirement). Passes the URL to redirect_handler and waits for callback_handler with waiting_on_a_person() (pausing the request clock). Verifies the returned state with secrets.compare_digest and validates the RFC 9207 iss parameter.
nodes.code:
pkce_params = PKCEParameters.generate()
state = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
auth_params = {
    "response_type": "code",
    "client_id": self.context.client_info.client_id,
    "redirect_uri": str(self.context.client_metadata.redirect_uris[0]),
    "state": state,
    "code_challenge": pkce_params.code_challenge,
    "code_challenge_method": "S256",
}
with waiting_on_a_person():
    await self.context.redirect_handler(authorization_url)
    result = await self.context.callback_handler()

nodes.name: _refresh_token()
nodes.summary: Builds a refresh_token grant request with the stored refresh token and returns it for the httpx2 generator to send.
nodes.detail: Reads the token endpoint from oauth_metadata or falls back to auth_base_url/token. Sends grant_type=refresh_token, the stored refresh_token, client_id, and optionally the RFC 8707 resource parameter. Calls prepare_token_auth() to add client credentials. The caller yields the returned request and passes the response to _handle_refresh_response(). On a non-200 response or a ValidationError the tokens are cleared and the method returns False, triggering full re-authentication.

nodes.name: _add_auth_header()
nodes.summary: Adds the Authorization: Bearer header to an outbound httpx2 request using the current access token.
nodes.detail: Called after a valid token is confirmed (either loaded from storage or freshly acquired). Sets request.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer <access_token>'. This is the only write to the outbound request; all other header manipulation happens inside the OAuth server responses.

nodes.name: Client auth exceptions
nodes.summary: Three exception classes covering OAuth flow failures, token errors and registration errors.
nodes.detail: OAuthFlowError is the base class. OAuthTokenError inherits from it and covers token exchange and refresh failures. OAuthRegistrationError covers dynamic client registration failures, including unusable registrations detected by check_registration_usable(). All are raised inside the _auth_flow generator and must be caught by callers.

nodes.name: OAuthFlowError
nodes.summary: Base exception for all client-side OAuth flow failures.

nodes.name: OAuthTokenError
nodes.summary: Raised when a token exchange or refresh request returns an error or invalid JSON.

nodes.name: OAuthRegistrationError
nodes.summary: Raised when dynamic client registration fails or returns unusable credentials.

nodes.name: Client auth utils
nodes.summary: Stateless helpers for OAuth metadata discovery, scope selection, issuer comparison, client registration and token response parsing.
nodes.detail: Twenty-two functions used by OAuthClientProvider._auth_flow(). Discovery helpers: build_protected_resource_metadata_discovery_urls(), build_oauth_authorization_server_metadata_discovery_urls(), create_oauth_metadata_request(), handle_protected_resource_response(), handle_auth_metadata_response(). Client management: create_client_registration_request(), handle_registration_response(), should_use_client_metadata_url(), create_client_info_from_metadata_url(), credentials_match_issuer(), is_valid_client_metadata_url(). Scope helpers: get_client_metadata_scopes(), union_scopes(). Issuer/issuer comparison: validate_metadata_issuer(), validate_authorization_response_iss(), issuers_match(). Header parsing: extract_field_from_www_auth(), extract_scope_from_www_auth(), extract_resource_metadata_from_www_auth(). Token response: handle_token_response_scopes().

nodes.name: build_prm_discovery_urls()
nodes.summary: Returns an ordered list of Protected Resource Metadata (PRM) URLs to try: WWW-Authenticate hint, path-based well-known, root well-known.
nodes.detail: Per SEP-985: (1) the resource_metadata URL from the WWW-Authenticate header if present; (2) /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource{path} when the server has a non-root path; (3) /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. The caller iterates these in order and stops on the first successful 200 response.
nodes.signature: def build_protected_resource_metadata_discovery_urls(www_auth_url: str | None, server_url: str) -> list[str]

nodes.name: get_client_metadata_scopes()
nodes.summary: Selects the effective scope for a token request using MCP spec priority: WWW-Authenticate, then PRM, then authorization-server metadata, then none.
nodes.detail: Also appends offline_access when the authorization server lists it in scopes_supported and the client's grant_types include refresh_token (SEP-2207). Called at step 3 of _auth_flow(). The returned scope string is set on client_metadata.scope before registration or token exchange.
nodes.signature: def get_client_metadata_scopes(www_authenticate_scope, protected_resource_metadata, authorization_server_metadata, client_grant_types) -> str | None

nodes.name: handle_registration_response()
nodes.summary: Parses a dynamic client registration response and returns OAuthClientInformationFull, stripping any server-echoed issuer field.
nodes.detail: Expects HTTP 200 or 201; raises OAuthRegistrationError on any other status. Parses the body with pydantic_core.from_json, pops any issuer key (the SDK stamps it, it must not be sourced from the wire), then validates into OAuthClientInformationFull. Both malformed JSON and validation errors surface as OAuthRegistrationError.

nodes.name: issuers_match()
nodes.summary: String-compares two issuer identifiers per RFC 8414, treating scheme://authority with and without a trailing slash as equal.
nodes.signature: def issuers_match(a: str, b: str) -> bool

nodes.name: Client OAuth extensions
nodes.summary: Machine-to-machine grant providers: client_credentials with client secret or private_key_jwt, and the SEP-990 identity-assertion grant.
nodes.detail: Three files. client_credentials.py provides ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider (client_id/client_secret) and PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider (JWT assertion), both extending OAuthClientProvider. identity_assertion.py provides IdentityAssertionOAuthProvider, a separate RedirectAwareAuth subclass that follows the SEP-990 ID-JAG flow against a fixed authorization server.

nodes.name: Client credentials extension
nodes.summary: OAuthClientProvider subclasses for the client_credentials grant: one using a client secret, one using a private_key_jwt assertion.
nodes.detail: ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider overrides _initialize() to inject a fixed OAuthClientInformationFull (skipping dynamic registration) and _perform_authorization() to call _exchange_token_client_credentials() which sends grant_type=client_credentials. PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider similarly overrides authorization but adds _add_client_authentication_jwt(), which calls the user-supplied assertion_provider callback with the discovered issuer as audience and adds client_assertion and client_assertion_type to the token request body (RFC 7523 §2.2). SignedJWTParameters provides a convenience create_assertion_provider() that signs a JWT with PyJWT. Both require an issuer argument; omitting it emits MCPDeprecationWarning.

nodes.name: ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider
nodes.summary: httpx2 auth provider for the OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant using a pre-configured client_id and client_secret.
nodes.detail: Extends OAuthClientProvider. Constructor sets a fixed OAuthClientInformationFull (grant_types=['client_credentials'], no redirect URIs) so discovery still runs but dynamic registration is skipped. Accepts client_id, client_secret, token_endpoint_auth_method (default client_secret_basic), scope and issuer. Overrides _select_authorization_server() to prefer the configured issuer in the PRM list.

nodes.name: PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider
nodes.summary: httpx2 auth provider for the OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant authenticating with a private_key_jwt assertion.
nodes.detail: Extends OAuthClientProvider. Requires an assertion_provider callback that takes the audience (authorization server issuer URL) and returns a signed JWT. The assertion is added to the token request as client_assertion with type urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer (RFC 7523 §2.2). Mints no client_secret and skips dynamic registration. SignedJWTParameters.create_assertion_provider() can supply the callback for testing.

nodes.name: Identity assertion extension
nodes.summary: SEP-990 leg-2 client provider that presents an Identity Assertion Authorization Grant (ID-JAG) to a configured authorization server.
nodes.detail: IdentityAssertionOAuthProvider extends RedirectAwareAuth directly (not OAuthClientProvider) because it never consults the resource server for authorization-server selection; the AS issuer is fixed at construction. On 401 or scope step-up it discovers ASM from the configured issuer's RFC 8414 well-known, verifies the token endpoint is on the same origin, calls assertion_provider(issuer, resource) for the ID-JAG, and POSTs grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer with the assertion. Confidential-client only: requires client_secret. No dynamic registration, no PRM discovery.

nodes.name: IdentityAssertionOAuthProvider
nodes.summary: httpx2 Auth for SEP-990 leg 2: presents an enterprise IdP-issued ID-JAG to the MCP authorization server via the RFC 7523 jwt-bearer grant.
nodes.detail: Constructor requires server_url, storage, client_id, client_secret (confidential client only), issuer (the AS), and assertion_provider callback. Maintains its own lock, token store and expiry. _auth_flow() discovers the token endpoint from the configured issuer's well-known, validates origin, calls assertion_provider(issuer, resource), POSTs the ID-JAG, stores the resulting token and retries the original request with the Bearer header. No redirect handlers and no PRM fetch.

nodes.name: Server auth provider protocol
nodes.summary: Protocol OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider that server implementations must satisfy, plus token and error data models.
nodes.detail: Defines the main protocol OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider[AuthorizationCodeT, RefreshTokenT, AccessTokenT] with eight required async methods: get_client, register_client, authorize, load_authorization_code, exchange_authorization_code, load_refresh_token, exchange_refresh_token, load_access_token, revoke_token, and exchange_identity_assertion (default raises TokenError unsupported). Also defines AuthorizationParams, IdentityAssertionParams, AuthorizationCode, RefreshToken, AccessToken (all Pydantic models), error types (RegistrationError, AuthorizeError, TokenError) with their literal error code types, and ProviderTokenVerifier (a TokenVerifier backed by a provider's load_access_token).

nodes.name: OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider
nodes.summary: Protocol an MCP server implements to provide full OAuth 2.0 authorization-server behavior: client lookup, authorization, token exchange and revocation.
nodes.detail: Generic over three token types (AuthorizationCodeT, RefreshTokenT, AccessTokenT). authorize() must return a redirect URL and must generate authorization codes with at least 160 bits of entropy. exchange_authorization_code() and exchange_refresh_token() should rotate both access and refresh tokens. revoke_token() should revoke both token types regardless of which is passed. exchange_identity_assertion() defaults to raising TokenError('unsupported_grant_type') and must be overridden to enable the SEP-990 ID-JAG grant.

nodes.name: AccessToken
nodes.summary: Pydantic model representing a verified access token: token string, client_id, scopes, optional expiry, resource indicator, subject and extra claims.
nodes.detail: Fields: token (str), client_id (str), scopes (list[str]), expires_at (int | None), resource (str | None, RFC 8707 indicator), subject (str | None, RFC 7662/9068 sub), claims (dict | None, additional claims like iss, act). Returned by TokenVerifier.verify_token() and OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider.load_access_token(). Bearer middleware checks expires_at and optionally resource against resource_server_url.

nodes.name: TokenVerifier
nodes.summary: Protocol with a single async verify_token() method: takes the raw bearer token and returns AccessToken | None.
nodes.detail: The integration surface for resource-server mode (as opposed to embedded authorization-server mode). Implementations call an introspection endpoint, verify a JWT, or look up a table. ProviderTokenVerifier is the backwards-compatible adapter that delegates to OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider.load_access_token().

nodes.name: principal_components()
nodes.summary: Returns (client_id, issuer, subject) from an AccessToken for session ownership and request-state binding.
nodes.signature: def principal_components(token: AccessToken) -> tuple[str, str | None, str | None]

nodes.name: Server auth settings
nodes.summary: AuthSettings, ClientRegistrationOptions and RevocationOptions: the flat configuration surface for the server-side OAuth integration.
nodes.detail: AuthSettings carries issuer_url (the AS URL), service_documentation_url, client_registration_options, revocation_options, required_scopes, identity_assertion_enabled (SEP-990), resource_server_url (the RS public URL for PRM), and validate_token_resource (whether bearer middleware checks AccessToken.resource against resource_server_url). A model_validator warns when resource_server_url is set but validate_token_resource is not, noting it will default to True in 3.0.
facts: validate_token_resource defaults to None; warn when resource_server_url is set without it
client_secret_expiry_seconds=None means client secrets never expire (0 sent in response per RFC 7591)
identity_assertion_enabled=False by default; must be set True to enable SEP-990

nodes.name: AuthSettings
nodes.summary: Pydantic model aggregating all authorization configuration for one MCP server: issuer, resource URL, scopes, registration and revocation options.

nodes.name: Server auth routes
nodes.summary: Assembles all Starlette OAuth routes, builds the well-known metadata document, and validates the issuer URL.
nodes.detail: create_auth_routes() instantiates one TokenHandler, one ClientAuthenticator and up to five Route objects: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, GET/POST /authorize, POST /token, POST /register (when enabled), POST /revoke (when enabled). Every route except /authorize is wrapped in CORS middleware; all POST routes are also wrapped in RequestBodyLimitMiddleware. build_metadata() derives OAuthMetadata from AuthSettings; it sets code_challenge_methods_supported=['S256'] and optionally adds registration_endpoint and revocation_endpoint. create_protected_resource_routes() builds the RFC 9728 /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/{path} route. validate_issuer_url() enforces HTTPS except for loopback addresses.
facts: AUTHORIZATION_PATH = '/authorize'
TOKEN_PATH = '/token'
REGISTRATION_PATH = '/register'
REVOCATION_PATH = '/revoke'
CORS allow_origins='*' on token, register and revoke endpoints

nodes.name: create_auth_routes()
nodes.summary: Builds and returns the list of Starlette Route objects for the OAuth 2.0 authorization server endpoints.
nodes.detail: Called by the MCPServer internals when an OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider is configured. Validates the issuer URL, constructs metadata via build_metadata(), creates a ClientAuthenticator and TokenHandler, then returns a list of Route objects. Registration and revocation routes are added only when their respective options are enabled.
nodes.signature: def create_auth_routes(provider, issuer_url, service_documentation_url, client_registration_options, revocation_options, identity_assertion_enabled) -> list[Route]
nodes.code:
routes = [
    Route("/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server",
          endpoint=cors_middleware(MetadataHandler(metadata).handle, ["GET", "OPTIONS"]),
          methods=["GET", "OPTIONS"]),
    Route(AUTHORIZATION_PATH,
          endpoint=_body_limited(request_response(AuthorizationHandler(provider).handle)),
          methods=["GET", "POST"]),
    Route(TOKEN_PATH,
          endpoint=_cors(_body_limited(request_response(token_handler.handle)), ["POST", "OPTIONS"]),
          methods=["POST", "OPTIONS"]),
]

nodes.name: build_metadata()
nodes.summary: Constructs the OAuthMetadata document served at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server from AuthSettings values.
nodes.signature: def build_metadata(issuer_url, service_documentation_url, client_registration_options, revocation_options, supports_identity_assertion) -> OAuthMetadata

nodes.name: create_protected_resource_routes()
nodes.summary: Creates a Starlette route for the RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata well-known endpoint.
nodes.detail: Builds a ProtectedResourceMetadata Pydantic model from the given resource_url and authorization_servers list, wraps it in ProtectedResourceMetadataHandler, and mounts it at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource{resource_path} (computed by build_resource_metadata_url). Called by MCPServer when resource_server_url is set.
nodes.signature: def create_protected_resource_routes(resource_url, authorization_servers, scopes_supported, resource_name, resource_documentation) -> list[Route]

nodes.name: Server auth handlers
nodes.summary: Five Starlette request handlers implementing the OAuth 2.0 authorization server endpoints.
nodes.detail: authorize.py handles GET/POST /authorize (authorization request validation and provider delegation). token.py handles POST /token (authorization_code, refresh_token and jwt-bearer grants). register.py handles POST /register (dynamic client registration). revoke.py handles POST /revoke (token revocation). metadata.py serves the well-known metadata and protected-resource-metadata documents.

nodes.name: Authorization handler
nodes.summary: Starlette handler for GET/POST /authorize: validates the authorization request, looks up the client and delegates the redirect decision to the provider.
nodes.detail: AuthorizationHandler.handle() parses query params (GET) or form data (POST) into AuthorizationRequest (Pydantic), validates client_id via provider.get_client(), validates redirect_uri and scope via OAuthClientInformationFull helpers, constructs AuthorizationParams including the RFC 8707 resource indicator, and calls provider.authorize() which returns the redirect URL. On any error it redirects to redirect_uri with error params if a valid client and redirect URI were resolved; otherwise returns JSON.
facts: code_challenge_method must be 'S256' (Literal enforced by Pydantic)
PKCE is mandatory: code_challenge is required (no default)

nodes.name: AuthorizationHandler
nodes.summary: Dataclass handler for the OAuth 2.0 /authorize endpoint, validating PKCE, client and scope before delegating to the provider.

nodes.name: Token handler
nodes.summary: Starlette handler for POST /token supporting authorization_code, refresh_token and jwt-bearer grant types.
nodes.detail: TokenHandler.handle() first authenticates the client via ClientAuthenticator.authenticate_request(), then parses the form into one of AuthorizationCodeRequest, RefreshTokenRequest or JwtBearerRequest using a discriminated union. For authorization_code: loads the code, checks expiry (RFC 6749 §10.5), verifies redirect_uri matches, verifies the PKCE code_verifier hash against the stored code_challenge, then calls provider.exchange_authorization_code(). For refresh_token: loads and validates, then calls provider.exchange_refresh_token(). For jwt-bearer (SEP-990): requires identity_assertion_enabled=True, requires a confidential client (client_secret present), builds IdentityAssertionParams and calls provider.exchange_identity_assertion().
facts: Authorization codes expire based on AuthorizationCode.expires_at compared to time.time()
PKCE verified by SHA-256 of code_verifier == code_challenge
jwt-bearer grant blocked for public clients (no client_secret)

nodes.name: TokenHandler
nodes.summary: Starlette handler for POST /token: authenticates the client, dispatches to the correct grant type handler, calls the provider and returns OAuthToken.
nodes.code:
match token_request:
    case AuthorizationCodeRequest():
        auth_code = await self.provider.load_authorization_code(client_info, token_request.code)
        sha256 = hashlib.sha256(token_request.code_verifier.encode()).digest()
        hashed_code_verifier = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(sha256).decode().rstrip("=")
        if hashed_code_verifier != auth_code.code_challenge:
            return self.response(TokenErrorResponse(error="invalid_grant", error_description="incorrect code_verifier"))
        tokens = await self.provider.exchange_authorization_code(client_info, auth_code)
    case RefreshTokenRequest():
        tokens = await self.provider.exchange_refresh_token(client_info, refresh_token, scopes)
    case JwtBearerRequest():
        tokens = await self.provider.exchange_identity_assertion(client_info, params)

nodes.name: Registration handler
nodes.summary: Starlette handler for POST /register: validates client metadata, generates credentials and calls provider.register_client().
nodes.detail: RegistrationHandler.handle() parses the JSON body into OAuthClientMetadata, enforces scope restrictions from ClientRegistrationOptions, generates a UUID client_id and a 32-byte hex client_secret (unless token_endpoint_auth_method='none'), sets client_secret_expires_at (0 for no expiry, a timestamp when expiry_seconds is configured, None for public clients), and calls provider.register_client(). Rejects private_key_jwt token_endpoint_auth_method and the JWT_BEARER_GRANT_TYPE in grant_types (ID-JAG clients must be pre-registered). Returns the full OAuthClientInformationFull as 201 JSON.
facts: client_id generated with str(uuid4())
client_secret is secrets.token_hex(32) for secret-based methods
private_key_jwt token_endpoint_auth_method is rejected with 400

nodes.name: RegistrationHandler
nodes.summary: Starlette handler for POST /register implementing RFC 7591 dynamic client registration.

nodes.name: Revocation handler
nodes.summary: Starlette handler for POST /revoke: authenticates the client, finds the token (access or refresh) and calls provider.revoke_token().
nodes.detail: RevocationHandler.handle() authenticates the client via ClientAuthenticator, parses the form into RevocationRequest (token, optional token_type_hint, client_id, client_secret). It tries load_access_token then load_refresh_token (or reversed when token_type_hint='refresh_token'), checks that the found token belongs to the authenticated client, and calls provider.revoke_token(). An unknown token returns HTTP 200 silently per RFC 7009.

nodes.name: RevocationHandler
nodes.summary: Starlette handler for POST /revoke implementing RFC 7009 token revocation.

nodes.name: Metadata handler
nodes.summary: Two Starlette handlers that serve pre-built OAuthMetadata and ProtectedResourceMetadata JSON documents.
nodes.detail: MetadataHandler wraps a pre-built OAuthMetadata and returns it as PydanticJSONResponse with Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 (1-hour cache). ProtectedResourceMetadataHandler does the same for ProtectedResourceMetadata. Both are dataclasses constructed by create_auth_routes() and create_protected_resource_routes() respectively.
facts: Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 on both metadata endpoints

nodes.name: MetadataHandler
nodes.summary: Serves the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata document at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.

nodes.name: ProtectedResourceMetadataHandler
nodes.summary: Serves the RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata document at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/{path}.

nodes.name: Server auth middleware
nodes.summary: Three Starlette ASGI middleware components for bearer-token verification, client authentication, and auth-context propagation.
nodes.detail: bearer_auth.py: BearerAuthBackend implements Starlette's AuthenticationBackend (token extraction and verification via TokenVerifier) and RequireAuthMiddleware enforces required scopes. client_auth.py: ClientAuthenticator validates client credentials on token and revoke requests. auth_context.py: AuthContextMiddleware stores the authenticated user in a contextvar for handler access via get_access_token().

nodes.name: Bearer auth middleware
nodes.summary: Starlette AuthenticationBackend and ASGI middleware that extract and verify Bearer tokens on every inbound HTTP request.
nodes.detail: BearerAuthBackend implements Starlette's AuthenticationBackend interface. authenticate() reads the Authorization header, strips 'Bearer ', calls TokenVerifier.verify_token(), checks expiry, and optionally checks that AccessToken.resource matches resource_server_url (URL comparison ignoring trailing slashes). Returns (AuthCredentials(scopes), AuthenticatedUser(access_token)) on success. RequireAuthMiddleware is a plain ASGI callable that checks the Starlette scope for an AuthenticatedUser and verifies every required scope; on failure it sends a 401 or 403 JSON response with a WWW-Authenticate header including the resource_metadata URL.
facts: Authorization header lookup is case-insensitive (iterates conn.headers)
token is conn.headers['Authorization'][7:] after prefix check
403 error value is 'insufficient_scope' (RFC 6750)

nodes.name: BearerAuthBackend
nodes.summary: Starlette AuthenticationBackend that delegates token verification to a TokenVerifier and optionally enforces the RFC 8707 resource indicator.

nodes.name: RequireAuthMiddleware
nodes.summary: ASGI middleware that halts requests lacking a valid Bearer token or the required scopes, responding with 401 or 403.

nodes.name: AuthenticatedUser
nodes.summary: Starlette SimpleUser subclass carrying the full AccessToken and its scopes after successful bearer verification.

nodes.name: Client auth middleware
nodes.summary: ClientAuthenticator validates client credentials on token and revoke requests, supporting client_secret_post, client_secret_basic and none methods.
nodes.detail: authenticate_request() reads client_id from form data, loads the client record via provider.get_client(), dispatches to Basic auth (Authorization header, URL-decoded, colon-split) or post auth (form field client_secret) or none. Uses hmac.compare_digest to avoid timing attacks on the secret. Raises AuthenticationError (not an HTTP exception; callers convert it to 401) on any failure including expired client_secret.
facts: hmac.compare_digest used for constant-time secret comparison
client_secret_expires_at checked against int(time.time())

nodes.name: ClientAuthenticator
nodes.summary: Validates client credentials on token-endpoint requests and returns the authenticated OAuthClientInformationFull.

nodes.name: Auth context middleware
nodes.summary: Stores the authenticated AccessToken in a contextvar so any handler can read it with get_access_token().
nodes.detail: auth_context_var is a ContextVar[AuthenticatedUser | None] with default None. AuthContextMiddleware.__call__() extracts the user from the ASGI scope, sets the contextvar, runs the inner app, and resets it in a finally block. get_access_token() returns user.access_token or None. Must sit after Starlette's AuthenticationMiddleware in the middleware stack.

nodes.name: get_access_token()
nodes.summary: Returns the AccessToken for the current request from the contextvar, or None outside an authenticated HTTP request.

nodes.name: AuthContextMiddleware
nodes.summary: ASGI middleware that propagates the authenticated user from the Starlette scope to the auth contextvar.

nodes.name: Server auth error helpers
nodes.summary: stringify_pydantic_error(): formats Pydantic validation errors into a human-readable dot-path: message string.
nodes.detail: One function: stringify_pydantic_error(ValidationError) joins each error's dot-path location with its message, producing a newline-separated string used as error_description in all handler error responses. This avoids leaking Pydantic's internal JSON format to OAuth clients.

nodes.name: Pydantic JSON response
nodes.summary: PydanticJSONResponse: JSONResponse subclass that serializes content via Pydantic's model_dump_json() with exclude_none=True.
nodes.detail: Starlette's JSONResponse uses json.dumps which cannot serialize AnyHttpUrl and other Pydantic URL types. PydanticJSONResponse.render() calls content.model_dump_json(exclude_none=True).encode('utf-8') instead, handling all Pydantic types correctly and stripping None fields from OAuth responses.

nodes.name: PydanticJSONResponse
nodes.summary: Starlette JSONResponse that serializes Pydantic models correctly by calling model_dump_json with exclude_none=True.

nodes.name: Shared OAuth models
nodes.summary: Pydantic models for RFC 6749/7591/8414/9728 OAuth tokens, client metadata, server metadata and resource metadata.
nodes.detail: OAuthToken (RFC 6749 §5.1): access_token, token_type (normalized to title case), expires_in, scope, refresh_token. OAuthClientMetadataBase: shared fields including grant_types (default authorization_code + refresh_token). OAuthClientMetadata: registration request type with redirect_uris (required, min 1), token_endpoint_auth_method, application_type (default native). OAuthClientInformationFull: registration response type; tolerates server-echoed nulls and empty strings via model_validator; has issuer field for SEP-2352 binding. OAuthMetadata (RFC 8414): issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint and many optional fields including client_id_metadata_document_supported and authorization_grant_profiles_supported. ProtectedResourceMetadata (RFC 9728): resource, authorization_servers (required min 1), bearer_methods_supported (default ['header']).

nodes.name: OAuthToken
nodes.summary: RFC 6749 §5.1 access-token response model: access_token, Bearer type, optional expires_in, scope and refresh_token.
nodes.detail: token_type is normalized to title case by field_validator so both 'bearer' and 'Bearer' (RFC 6750 §4) are stored as 'Bearer'. expires_in is stored as-is; OAuthContext.update_token_expiry() converts it to an absolute timestamp via calculate_token_expiry().

nodes.name: OAuthClientInformationFull
nodes.summary: RFC 7591 §3.2.1 client registration response: all client metadata plus client_id, optional client_secret and SDK-added issuer binding.
nodes.detail: model_validator _placeholder_members_read_as_omitted() strips null and empty-string values before parsing so a server echoing unset members as null does not reject an otherwise valid record. The issuer field (not an RFC 7591 field) is stamped by the SDK after a successful registration to bind credentials to the authorization server they were registered with (SEP-2352). validate_scope() and validate_redirect_uri() are helper methods used by the authorization handler.

nodes.name: OAuthMetadata
nodes.summary: RFC 8414 OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata including fields for PKCE, OIDC, SEP-990 and client-id metadata document support.

nodes.name: ProtectedResourceMetadata
nodes.summary: RFC 9728 OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata: resource URL, authorization server list, scopes and bearer method support.
nodes.detail: resource and authorization_servers (required, min 1) are the only required fields. bearer_methods_supported defaults to ['header'] because MCP only supports header-based bearer tokens. All other fields are optional. Used by both the server (to build the well-known document) and the client (to parse it during discovery).

nodes.name: Shared auth utils
nodes.summary: Three pure utility functions for RFC 8707 resource URL canonicalization, hierarchical resource matching, and token expiry calculation.
nodes.detail: resource_url_from_server_url() strips the fragment, lowercases scheme and host, leaving the path intact (RFC 8707 §2). check_resource_allowed() compares origin (scheme, netloc) exactly and checks that the requested path starts with the configured path after normalizing trailing slashes; this enables a token for a parent resource to cover child paths. calculate_token_expiry() converts an expires_in integer to a Unix timestamp with time.time(), or returns None if expires_in is absent.

nodes.name: resource_url_from_server_url()
nodes.summary: Returns a canonical RFC 8707 resource URI: lowercase scheme and host, no fragment.
nodes.signature: def resource_url_from_server_url(url: str | HttpUrl | AnyUrl) -> str

nodes.name: check_resource_allowed()
nodes.summary: Returns True if requested_resource shares the same origin as configured_resource and its path is a hierarchical child.

nodes.name: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
nodes.summary: Returns the RFC 8414 OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata document as JSON.
nodes.detail: Assembled by create_auth_routes() in routes.py using MetadataHandler. Wrapped in CORS middleware (allow_origins='*', methods GET/OPTIONS). Served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600. The document lists issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, and optionally registration_endpoint and revocation_endpoint. No routes.py service declaration; this is an inferred endpoint assembled from named constants in routes.py.

nodes.name: GET /authorize
nodes.summary: Authorization endpoint (RFC 6749 §4.1.1): receives the authorization request and redirects to the provider-chosen URL.
nodes.detail: Also accepts POST. Assembled in create_auth_routes() using AuthorizationHandler. CORS is intentionally omitted (comment in routes.py: clients should redirect, not XHR). Body size is limited by RequestBodyLimitMiddleware. Requires PKCE (code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256). Returns a 302 redirect to the URL returned by provider.authorize(), or a 302/400 error on validation failure. No routes.py service declaration; assembled from AUTHORIZATION_PATH='/authorize' in routes.py.

nodes.name: POST /token
nodes.summary: Token endpoint (RFC 6749 §4.1.3): exchanges an authorization code, refresh token or JWT bearer grant for an access token.
nodes.detail: Assembled in create_auth_routes() using TokenHandler. Wrapped in CORS and body-limit middleware. Accepts authorization_code, refresh_token and (when identity_assertion_enabled) urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer grant types. Authenticates the client via ClientAuthenticator before dispatching to the grant handler. No routes.py service declaration; assembled from TOKEN_PATH='/token' in routes.py.

nodes.name: POST /register
nodes.summary: Dynamic client registration (RFC 7591 §3.1): registers a new client and returns its credentials.
nodes.detail: Added by create_auth_routes() only when ClientRegistrationOptions.enabled=True. Uses RegistrationHandler. Wrapped in CORS and body-limit middleware. Rejects private_key_jwt and the JWT bearer grant type. Returns 201 with the full OAuthClientInformationFull including the generated client_id and client_secret. No routes.py service declaration; assembled from REGISTRATION_PATH='/register' in routes.py.

nodes.name: POST /revoke
nodes.summary: Token revocation (RFC 7009): authenticates the client and calls provider.revoke_token() on the submitted token.
nodes.detail: Added by create_auth_routes() only when RevocationOptions.enabled=True. Uses RevocationHandler. Wrapped in CORS and body-limit middleware. Returns 200 regardless of whether the token was found (per RFC 7009). No routes.py service declaration; assembled from REVOCATION_PATH='/revoke' in routes.py.

nodes.name: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/{path}
nodes.summary: RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata: tells clients which authorization servers can issue tokens for this resource.
nodes.detail: Assembled by create_protected_resource_routes() using ProtectedResourceMetadataHandler. The path includes the resource server's path component per RFC 9728 §3.1 (e.g. /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp for resource https://example.com/mcp). Wrapped in CORS. Served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600. No routes.py service declaration; path computed by build_resource_metadata_url() in routes.py.

nodes.name: build_asm_discovery_urls()
nodes.summary: Returns an ordered list of Authorization Server Metadata (ASM) well-known URLs to try: path-based OAuth, path-based OIDC, root OAuth, root OIDC.
nodes.detail: Called at step 2 of _auth_flow() with the authorization server URL discovered from PRM. Generates up to four candidates per RFC 8414 and OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server{path}, /.well-known/openid-configuration{path}, {path}/.well-known/openid-configuration, then root variants. Without an auth_server_url (legacy 2025-03-26 spec) it falls back to the MCP server's own origin.
nodes.signature: def build_oauth_authorization_server_metadata_discovery_urls(auth_server_url: str | None, server_url: str) -> list[str]
nodes.code:
if not auth_server_url:
    parsed = urlparse(server_url)
    return [f"{parsed.scheme}://{parsed.netloc}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server"]
urls: list[str] = []
parsed = urlparse(auth_server_url)
base_url = f"{parsed.scheme}://{parsed.netloc}"
if parsed.path and parsed.path != "/":
    oauth_path = f"/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server{parsed.path.rstrip('/')}"
    urls.append(urljoin(base_url, oauth_path))
    oidc_path = f"/.well-known/openid-configuration{parsed.path.rstrip('/')}"
    urls.append(urljoin(base_url, oidc_path))
    oidc_path = f"{parsed.path.rstrip('/')}/.well-known/openid-configuration"
    urls.append(urljoin(base_url, oidc_path))
    return urls

nodes.name: extract_resource_metadata_from_www_auth()
nodes.summary: Extracts the resource_metadata URL from a 401 or 403 WWW-Authenticate header per RFC 9728.
nodes.detail: Returns None if the response is absent, is not 401 or 403, or if resource_metadata is not present in the WWW-Authenticate header. Delegates to extract_field_from_www_auth() for the actual regex parsing. Called at the start of step 1 in _auth_flow() to get the PRM hint URL.

nodes.name: union_scopes()
nodes.summary: Merges two space-delimited scope strings, preserving order and deduplicating, for step-up re-authorization per SEP-2350.
nodes.detail: Called when a 403 insufficient_scope response arrives with a new scope challenge. Splits both strings, appends new scopes not already in the previous set, and returns a single space-joined string. Preserves the order of previously requested scopes so authorization for prior operations is not dropped.
nodes.signature: def union_scopes(previous_scope: str | None, new_scope: str | None) -> str | None

nodes.name: create_oauth_metadata_request()
nodes.summary: Builds an httpx2 GET Request for a well-known metadata URL with the MCP protocol version header attached.
nodes.detail: Returns a Request('GET', url, headers={MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION_HEADER: LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION}). The header notifies the authorization server of the client's MCP version, allowing servers to adjust metadata responses for newer protocol features (SEP-2468). Called by _auth_flow() for each URL in the discovery URL lists.

nodes.name: calculate_token_expiry()
nodes.summary: Converts an expires_in seconds value to an absolute Unix timestamp using time.time(), or returns None when expires_in is absent.
nodes.detail: Called by OAuthContext.update_token_expiry() after a successful token exchange or refresh. Handles servers that return expires_in as a string by coercing to int. Returns None for a None input (pragma: no cover on that branch).
nodes.signature: def calculate_token_expiry(expires_in: int | str | None) -> float | None

nodes.name: ProviderTokenVerifier
nodes.summary: Backwards-compatible TokenVerifier implementation that delegates verify_token() to an OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider.load_access_token().
nodes.detail: Wraps any OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider in the TokenVerifier protocol. Provided for servers that use embedded authorization-server mode; for AS/RS separation a dedicated verifier (such as IntrospectionTokenVerifier) is preferred. Implements the TokenVerifier protocol by calling provider.load_access_token(token).

nodes.name: OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider.authorize()
nodes.summary: Protocol method that handles the /authorize request and returns a redirect URL; implementations typically chain to a third-party OAuth server.
nodes.detail: Takes an OAuthClientInformationFull and AuthorizationParams (including PKCE challenge, state, redirect_uri, scope, and RFC 8707 resource indicator). Must return a URL to redirect the client to. The comment in provider.py illustrates the typical three-party pattern: client talks to MCP server, MCP server talks to a third-party OAuth server, and the authorization code is returned through redirect_uri. Implementations must generate authorization codes with at least 160 bits of entropy.
nodes.signature: async def authorize(self, client: OAuthClientInformationFull, params: AuthorizationParams) -> str

nodes.name: OAuthASProvider.exchange_authorization_code()
nodes.summary: Protocol method that exchanges a verified authorization code for an OAuthToken containing access and refresh tokens.
nodes.detail: Called by TokenHandler after PKCE verification and expiry checks pass. Should rotate both the access and refresh tokens on each exchange to prevent replay attacks. Raises TokenError on any validation failure. The returned OAuthToken is serialized and sent to the client.
nodes.signature: async def exchange_authorization_code(self, client: OAuthClientInformationFull, authorization_code: AuthorizationCodeT) -> OAuthToken

nodes.name: TokenHandler.handle()
nodes.summary: Authenticates the client, dispatches to the correct grant handler, calls the provider and returns an OAuthToken response.
nodes.detail: Entry point for POST /token. Authenticates the client via ClientAuthenticator.authenticate_request(); on failure returns 401 invalid_client. Parses form data into a discriminated union (AuthorizationCodeRequest | RefreshTokenRequest | JwtBearerRequest). For authorization_code: verifies code expiry, validates redirect_uri, verifies PKCE, then calls provider.exchange_authorization_code(). For refresh_token: validates scope subset, calls provider.exchange_refresh_token(). For jwt-bearer: requires identity_assertion_enabled and a confidential client, then calls provider.exchange_identity_assertion(). All token and error responses carry Cache-Control: no-store.
nodes.signature: async def handle(self, request: Request) -> Response

flows.name: Client hits 401, runs authorization-code flow, retries
flows.summary: An unauthenticated client request triggers OAuth 2.0 authorization-code discovery and token exchange before retrying.

steps.text: httpx2 invokes _auth_flow(). No valid token is found in OAuthContext. The original request is forwarded without an Authorization header.

The server's RequireAuthMiddleware finds no AuthenticatedUser in the ASGI scope (BearerAuthBackend returned None for the missing header) and returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate containing resource_metadata URL.

Step 1: the client extracts resource_metadata from WWW-Authenticate and builds an ordered list of PRM discovery URLs. It yields GET requests until a 200 response parses into ProtectedResourceMetadata, recording the authorization server URL.

Step 2: the client builds an ordered list of well-known URLs for the discovered authorization server. It yields GET requests until OAuthMetadata is parsed. validate_metadata_issuer() verifies the issuer matches expectations (RFC 8414 §3.3 / SEP-2468).
Step 3: scope is selected from WWW-Authenticate, PRM scopes_supported, or ASM scopes_supported in priority order; offline_access is appended when the AS supports refresh_token (SEP-2207).

Step 4: the client POSTs its OAuthClientMetadata to the registration endpoint. The server generates a UUID client_id and 32-byte hex client_secret, stores them via provider.register_client() and returns 201. check_registration_usable() verifies the credentials are usable.

Step 5a: the client generates PKCEParameters and a random state token, constructs the authorization URL and calls redirect_handler with it. It then awaits callback_handler (request clock paused by waiting_on_a_person). The returned code and state are verified with secrets.compare_digest.

Step 5b: the client POSTs the authorization code and code_verifier to /token. The server verifies PKCE (SHA-256(verifier) == stored challenge) and calls provider.exchange_authorization_code(), returning an OAuthToken.
The token is stored via TokenStorage.set_tokens(). _add_auth_header() attaches Authorization: Bearer to the original request, which is re-yielded and succeeds.

flows.name: Authenticated request verified by bearer middleware
flows.summary: An inbound HTTP request with a Bearer token passes through the middleware stack to the MCP handler after token verification.

steps.text: Starlette's AuthenticationMiddleware calls BearerAuthBackend.authenticate(). It reads the Authorization header case-insensitively, strips the 'Bearer ' prefix, and passes the raw token to TokenVerifier.verify_token().

The application-supplied TokenVerifier (e.g. a JWT validator or introspection client) returns an AccessToken with client_id, scopes, expires_at, resource and optional subject and claims, or None if the token is invalid.

BearerAuthBackend checks expires_at against the current time and optionally compares AccessToken.resource against resource_server_url. On success it returns (AuthCredentials(scopes), AuthenticatedUser(access_token)) to Starlette.
RequireAuthMiddleware finds the AuthenticatedUser in the ASGI scope and verifies every required scope is in AuthCredentials.scopes. Missing scopes return 403 with error=insufficient_scope.

AuthContextMiddleware sets auth_context_var to the AuthenticatedUser for the duration of the request. Any MCP handler can call get_access_token() to read the AccessToken without threading it through call arguments.
